newsitem.title: CANADA: Thiessen says rate cuts effect to be felt in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Thiessen says rate cuts effect to be felt in 1997.

text.p: Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen said on Tuesday the impact of the Bank's agressive easing of monetary policy, which began in the spring of 1995, would only be felt in 1997 and thereafter.

"There does tend to be a rather long lag in the impact of monetary policy... And so the effects of the declining interest rates over the last year are really only going to be felt during the course of 1997 and beyond," Thiessen told members of the House of Commons Finance Committee during questions after his semi-annual testimony in parliament.
"And it is during that period that we expect to see a pickup in economic activity and an improvement in employment," Thiessen added.
Thiessen also said the relatively low interest rates the Bank has set over the past few quarters were needed to boost Canada's sluggish economic growth.
"Right now we need relatively low interest rates to help the economy get going. And I think that it's probably in everybody's interest that it gets going," Thiessen said.
Thiessen's testimony followed the release of the Bank of Canada's semi-annual Monetary Policy Report two weeks ago. --Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745
"I don't think that this export industry is just on the verge of decline if there is a slight uptick in the Canadian dollar," Thiessen said.
In fact, he suggested that a rise in Canada's imports in recent months meant the economy was beginning to strengthen.
